name: Euroscepticism
summary: Euroscepticism is opposition to the European Union or to the direction of European integration. In the standard scholarly typology, hard Euroscepticism opposes the EU and the whole project on principle, wants a loose intergovernmental Europe of fully sovereign states or withdrawal, and soft Euroscepticism accepts membership but opposes the extension of EU powers where national interest is at odds with them. Scholars stress that it is defined by this one stance and is attached to many other ideologies (nationalism, socialism, populism, conservatism), so its sources record no common position outside sovereignty and integration.
scope: Euroscepticism as the defining scholarship states it: Szczerbiak and Taggart's hard and soft Euroscepticism (s6, s5, s2), the hard ideal type as restated by Hloušek and Havlík (s7), and the consensus on those definitions (s9). Answers come only from those accounts of what the stance holds. The positions of parties and leaders who hold it (UKIP, AfD, Thatcher, Syriza, Die Linke and others) are other subjects' and are not used, so nothing is taken from their programmes or speeches.
